Baltimore Sonic Research Institute browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Baltimore Sonic Research Institute Radical Conversion - Discrete Opamp Distortion Published on March 8, 2026 Baltimore Sonic Research Institute distortion pedal Information The Radical Conversion is a distortion pedal by Baltimore Sonic Research Institute that recreates the core architecture of the Boss Metal Zone style circuit using fully discrete transistor-based opamp stages rather than integrated circuits. The design originated from a project in which the developer analyzed and rebuilt multiple Boss analog distortion pedals that used discrete opamp circuits. These circuits, first introduced in the Boss OD-2 in 1985, have appeared in numerous Boss models including the BD-2, OD-3, and FZ-2, as well as less common pedals such as the MZ-2, PW-2, and MD-2. Radical Conversion adapts that design philosophy by replacing conventional integrated opamps with discrete transistor implementations. The pedal employs multiple discrete opamp architectures, including the classic Boss-style design, resulting in a circuit constructed from 27 transistors. This approach intentionally substitutes lower performance integrated amplifiers with discrete stages that introduce additional harmonic complexity when driven into distortion. The overall concept is a discrete reinterpretation of the Metal Zone topology, including its active semi-parametric midrange equalizer and multi-stage gain structure. All amplification and filtering stages are implemented with discrete transistor circuits, and the equalization section mirrors the active tone shaping associated with the original Metal Zone design. The circuit has been adjusted to reflect contemporary tonal preferences, and the pedal adds three selectable preamp voicings that alter the signal entering the main gain stage. These voicing modes allow the input signal to emphasize different frequency ranges before distortion, affecting both the response and compression characteristics of the pedal. The first voicing reproduces the traditional Metal Zone style preamp boost, emphasizing midrange frequencies prior to the gain stage.
